html:
Sohar is a port on the Batinah coast of Oman that was one of the busiest harbours of the Indian Ocean in the 10th century. Geographers of the time called it the gateway to China.

Its merchants traded with Basra, India, East Africa and southern China, carrying horses, dates and copper out and bringing back spices, cloth and porcelain. Its houses were of brick and teak, and it was the largest town of Oman. Omanis like to say it was the home of Sindbad the sailor of the Thousand and One Nights.

Sohar declined from the 11th century as Hormuz and later Muscat took its trade. It has revived as a modern industrial port. See also Ahmad ibn Majid.
